evals.prompt: List the five severity levels the AWS CloudTrail cost optimization skill uses for its findings, in order from most to least urgent. No account access required.
evals.expected_output: Lists CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFO in that order.
assertions: The five severity levels are given in order from most to least urgent (CRITICAL first, INFO last)

evals.prompt: According to the AWS CloudTrail cost optimization skill, are CloudTrail data events ever free? And is the first copy of management events per Region free? No account access required.
evals.expected_output: States that the first copy of management events per Region is free, but data events are never free - every data event delivery is billed.
assertions: The response states the first copy of management events per Region is free
The response addresses CloudTrail data events
The response states that data events are never free or are always billed

evals.prompt: In us-east-1 I have two trails both logging All management events: a multi-Region organization trail (org-multi-region-trail) and a separate single-Region trail (legacy-security-trail). Which one is the paid duplicate, and what is the recommended fix? Explain briefly why, based on CloudTrail's free-copy rule. No account access required.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the single-Region legacy-security-trail as the paid duplicate because the multi-Region org trail already delivers the free first copy of management events in every Region, and recommends turning off management event logging on the single-Region trail (or converting it to data-events-only) rather than deleting the authoritative multi-Region trail.
assertions: The response identifies the single-Region trail (legacy-security-trail) as the paid duplicate
The response explains the fix in terms of a duplicate or paid second copy of management events
The response references CloudTrail's free first copy rule for management events
The response keeps the multi-Region/authoritative trail rather than recommending deleting it

evals.prompt: I plan to de-duplicate down to a single management-event trail, and I also want to exclude KMS and RDS Data API events from that surviving trail to save money. Is excluding those events from the sole remaining trail a real cost saving? Explain, based on how CloudTrail bills management events. No account access required.
evals.expected_output: Explains that once you are down to a single management-event trail, that trail's management events are the free first copy per Region, so excluding KMS/RDS from it saves ~$0 on management events and instead removes those events from the only trail capturing them - a coverage/audit gap, not a saving. KMS/RDS exclusion only saves money on a paid (second-or-later) copy that is deliberately kept; de-duplication and management-event filtering should not be stacked as additive savings on the same copy.
assertions: The response states that the single surviving trail's management events are the free first copy, so excluding KMS/RDS from it does not save money
The response warns that excluding those events from the sole trail creates a coverage/audit gap rather than a saving
The response notes that management-event exclusion only saves money on a paid (second-or-later) copy, not the single authoritative trail

evals.prompt: For an AWS CloudTrail cost optimization review of account 123456789012, state the report artifact filename you would generate (use today's date in YYYY-MM-DD form). Do not run the review.
evals.expected_output: Proposes an artifact name of the form cloudtrail-cost-optimization-123456789012-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md.

assertions.text: The response proposes an artifact filename of the form cloudtrail-cost-optimization-<account-id>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md

evals.prompt: Help me write an S3 bucket policy that grants a specific IAM role read-only access to one prefix.
evals.expected_output: The CloudTrail cost optimization skill should not activate - this is an S3 bucket policy authoring request unrelated to CloudTrail cost.
assertions: The response addresses writing an S3 bucket policy and does not steer the user into a CloudTrail cost optimization review
